answer.evidence: The trained layer-1 units fall into two mirror-image families of centred, radially symmetric filters. Ring units (1, 6, 9, 10, 11, 12, 16, 27, 30) have strong positive weights (about +40 to +95) on an annulus spanning roughly rows 5-18 and cols 5-18. They have a negative core at rows 11-13, cols 11-13, and weak or negative surround. Centre-surround units (0, 3, 5, 8, 14, 15, 18, 20, 23, 24, 25, 28, 31) show the opposite pattern: a positive core (e.g. unit 0 r11c12 = 82, unit 23 r11c12 = 99), a negative annulus, and broadly positive periphery. Unit 19 is uniformly positive and acts like a bias or total-brightness unit. Units 2, 4, 7, 13, 17, 21, 22, 26, 29 look like near-initialisation noise (|w| < ~35). Layer 2 combines these by family. u4 (output weight +99) takes +55, +74, +66, +52 from ring units 1, 6, 9, 30 and -63, -87, -82, -71 from centre units 0, 14, 24, 25. u9 (output weight -98) and u3 (output weight -93) mostly take positive input from centre units (e.g. u9: unit 14 +94, unit 24 +87, unit 5 +85). I scanned all corners and edges for a compact block of large, same-sign weights shared across units and found none. The periphery weights are spread roughly evenly around the whole border and look like bias-like drift. A few scattered outer pixels (e.g. r10c22, r16c21, r20c19, r8c2) do get consistently signed weights across units, but they are isolated single pixels on a ring of radius ~10-12, not a localized patch. They also follow each unit's family sign, which fits finite-sample noise correlation rather than a planted feature.
answer.main_feature: The model compares brightness on a mid-radius annulus around the image centre (radius ~4-8 px, lit only by large blobs) against brightness at the very centre. Ring detectors push toward 'large'; centre-surround detectors (bright core, dark annulus) push toward 'small'.
